examples.en: Today I ordered gochujapchae and flower buns at the Chinese restaurant.
Gochujapchae is delicious with rice too.

examples.ko: 집에서 고추잡채를 만들어 보려고 재료를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought ingredients to try making gochujapchae at home.
I finely sliced the bell peppers that go into gochujapchae.
How about gochujapchae for dinner tonight?
Please give us one more plate of gochujapchae.

explain: 한국식 중국집 메뉴로, 보통 꽃빵과 함께 나와요. 이름이 '잡채'로 끝나지만 당면이 아니라 고기와 채소를 가늘게 썰어 볶은 요리예요.
explain_en: It is a Korean-Chinese restaurant dish usually served with flower buns. Although the name ends in '잡채', it is shredded meat and vegetables stir-fried, not glass noodles.

en: gulbi; salted and dried yellow croaker

examples.en: I received Yeonggwang gulbi as a holiday gift.
Gulbi is yellow croaker that has been salted and dried.

examples.ko: 밥 위에 굴비 살을 올려 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: It's delicious to eat gulbi flesh on top of rice.

examples.ko: 할머니가 프라이팬에 굴비를 노릇하게 구워 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother grilled gulbi to a golden brown in the pan.
A gulbi set meal is a little expensive.

examples.ko: 냉동실에 굴비가 두 마리 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Two gulbi are left in the freezer.

explain: '굴비'는 조기를 소금에 절여 말린 생선이에요. 그냥 '조기'는 말리기 전의 신선한 생선을 부를 때 쓰고, '굴비'는 말린 뒤의 이름이에요. 전라도 영광 굴비가 유명해서 명절 선물로 인기가 많아요.
explain_en: 굴비 is a yellow croaker that has been salted and dried. The fresh fish before drying is called 조기, and 굴비 is the name after drying. Yeonggwang in Jeolla is famous for it, so it is a popular holiday gift.

examples.en: I put meat and green onions on the skewer.
I walked while eating skewers at the night market.
The skewer is hot, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 꼬치는 매운 소스를 찍어 먹어요.
examples.en: You dip this skewer in spicy sauce.

examples.ko: 친구가 나무 꼬치에 과일을 꽂아 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend put fruit on a wooden skewer for me.
It's two thousand won per skewer.

explain: '닭꼬치', '양꼬치', '어묵 꼬치'처럼 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 불러요. 음식도 꼬치이고 음식을 꿰는 막대도 꼬치예요. 셀 때는 '꼬치 하나', '꼬치 두 개'라고 해요.
explain_en: Put the ingredient first, as in 닭꼬치 (chicken), 양꼬치 (lamb), and 어묵 꼬치 (fish cake). 꼬치 is both the food and the stick it is threaded on, and you count them as '꼬치 하나', '꼬치 두 개'.

examples.en: I caught a big sea bass fishing.
Raw sea bass is chewy and clean-tasting.

examples.ko: 오늘 시장에서 농어를 한 마리 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought one sea bass at the market today.

examples.ko: 농어는 바다와 강이 만나는 곳에서도 살아요.
examples.en: Sea bass also live where the sea meets a river.
My grandfather makes spicy sea bass stew very well.

examples.ko: 여름에는 농어 낚시를 하러 바닷가에 가요.
examples.en: In summer I go to the seaside for sea bass fishing.

explain: 농어는 여름이 제철인 바다 흰살 생선이라 횟집에서 자주 봐요. 겨울이 제철인 '숭어'와 철이 달라요. 이름이 비슷한 '송어'는 연어 종류의 민물고기라서 농어와 전혀 달라요.
explain_en: 농어 is a white-fleshed sea fish at its best in summer, so you often see it at raw-fish restaurants. 숭어 is at its best in winter, so the seasons differ. 송어, with a similar name, is a salmon-family freshwater fish and quite different from 농어.

examples.en: The stadium was a cauldron of excitement with the sound of cheering.
In winter, I crave ox knee-cartilage soup.

examples.ko: 대학 축제는 노래와 춤으로 열광의 도가니가 되었어요.
examples.en: The college festival turned into a frenzy of singing and dancing.

examples.ko: 금속을 녹이려고 도가니에 넣고 불을 붙였어요.
examples.en: To melt the metal, I put it in a crucible and lit the fire.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 여러 문화가 섞인 도가니 같아요.
examples.en: This city is like a melting pot where many cultures mix.

examples.ko: 실험실에서 쓰는 도가니는 높은 열에도 깨지지 않아요.
examples.en: The crucible used in the lab doesn't break even in high heat.

explain: 일상에서는 '흥분의 도가니', '열광의 도가니'처럼 분위기가 뜨겁게 끓는 장면에서 가장 많이 들어요. 식당 메뉴의 '도가니탕'은 소 무릎 부위로 끓인 국이에요.

phrases.example: 결승골이 터지자 관중석이 흥분의 도가니에 빠졌어요.
phrases.en: When the winning goal went in, the stands were thrown into a frenzy of excitement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 사람이 한꺼번에 흥분해서 들끓는 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an atmosphere in which many people are excited all at once and the place seems to boil.

explain_en: In daily life you hear it most in scenes where the mood is boiling, as in '흥분의 도가니' and '열광의 도가니'. '도가니탕' on a restaurant menu is a soup made from the knee part of a cow.

examples.en: The peach was very soft, so I ate it right away.
This bread is soft and moist.
When persimmons get soft, they are sweet and tasty.
The rice turned out mushy.
I tend to like soft jelly.
The ground was soaked by rain and soft.

explain: '말랑말랑하다'는 보통 기분 좋은 부드러움이고, '물렁물렁하다'는 단단해야 할 것이 너무 무르다는 느낌으로도 많이 써요. 과일, 밥, 젖은 땅 등에 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '말랑말랑하다' usually sounds pleasantly soft, while '물렁물렁하다' is often used when something that should be firm is too soft. It is common for fruit, rice and wet ground.

examples.en: The fruit came out piled attractively on the plate.

examples.ko: 소담한 한 상을 차려 주셔서 감사해요.
examples.en: Thank you for setting such a lovely, generous table.

examples.ko: 꽃이 소담해서 보기만 해도 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: The flowers are so full and lovely that just looking at them cheers me up.
This is a pleasant, neat Korean restaurant.

examples.ko: 엄마가 싸 주신 도시락은 작지만 소담했어요.
examples.en: The lunchbox Mom packed was small but looked lovely and full.
The table isn't lavish, but I prepared it with care.

explain: 음식, 꽃, 열매처럼 모양이 탐스럽고 보기 좋을 때 써요. '푸짐하다'가 양이 많은 데 초점이라면 '소담하다'는 보기 좋게 넉넉한 느낌이 있어요. 대화보다는 식당 소개나 글에서 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when food, flowers or fruit look full and pleasing. While '푸짐하다' focuses on large quantity, '소담하다' adds a pleasant, generous look. It fits restaurant introductions and writing better than casual talk.

examples.en: The biggest pleasure of traveling is enjoying food.
I went on a food trip to Busan.

examples.ko: 식도락을 즐기는 편이라 맛집을 많이 알아요.
examples.en: I enjoy eating out, so I know a lot of good restaurants.
Since I got into food exploring, I've gained weight.

examples.ko: 제 취미는 식도락이라서 주말마다 새 식당에 가요.
examples.en: My hobby is food exploring, so I go to a new restaurant every weekend.
This city is famous for its food scene.

explain: 맛있는 음식을 찾아 먹으며 즐기는 일이나 취미를 말해요. '식도락 여행', '식도락을 즐기다'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '맛집 투어'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the hobby or pleasure of seeking out and enjoying good food. It is often used as '식도락 여행' or '식도락을 즐기다'. In daily talk people also say '맛집 투어'.

examples.en: This glutinous rice cake is really chewy and sticky.
If the dough is sticky, it clings to your hands.
I like sticky rice.
The rice cake was stickier than I expected.
I want to eat sticky, chewy rice cake.

examples.ko: 쌀을 바꿨더니 밥이 더 차져서 맛있어요.
examples.en: After changing the rice, the cooked rice got stickier and tastier.

explain: 밥, 떡, 반죽처럼 끈기가 있어서 달라붙는 느낌일 때 써요. 비슷한 '쫄깃하다'는 씹는 맛이 탄력 있다는 쪽이라 차지다와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '차진 밥'처럼 -ㄴ으로 꾸미는 형태를 자주 써요.
explain_en: Used for food like rice, rice cake, or dough that has a sticky, clingy texture. 쫄깃하다 focuses on the bouncy chew, and the two often appear together. The modifier form '차진' (as in 차진 밥) is very common.

examples.en: My friend gave me sticky rice cakes the day before the exam.
There is sweet red bean filling inside the rice cake.

examples.ko: 찹쌀떡은 목에 걸리지 않게 천천히 드세요.
examples.en: Eat the rice cake slowly so it doesn't get stuck in your throat.
Rice cakes with strawberry inside are popular.
The rice cake hardened, so I heated it in the microwave.
I ate two rice cakes as a snack.

explain: 찹쌀로 만든 쫀득한 떡이고 속에 팥이나 과일을 넣은 것이 흔해요. 시험 전에 '붙으라'는 뜻으로 찹쌀떡을 선물하는 문화가 있어요. 아주 쫀득하니 목에 걸리지 않게 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: This is a chewy rice cake made from glutinous rice, often filled with red bean paste or fruit. There is a custom of giving it before exams, as a wish that one will 'stick' (pass). It is very sticky, so be careful not to choke.

examples.en: Castella is soft and sweet, so kids like it.
I had castella and milk for breakfast.

examples.ko: 이 집 카스텔라가 촉촉해서 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: This shop's castella is moist and really delicious.

examples.ko: 커피랑 같이 카스텔라 한 조각만 주세요.
examples.en: Please give me just one slice of castella with a coffee.
I want to try baking castella at home.
This morning I spread strawberry jam on my castella and ate it.

explain: 표준 표기는 '카스텔라'지만 말할 때는 '카스테라'라고 하는 사람도 있어요. 빵집이나 편의점 빵 코너에서 흔히 보여요. 자를 때는 '한 조각', '한 쪽'으로 세요.
explain_en: The standard spelling is '카스텔라', but some people say '카스테라' in speech. You often see it in bakeries and convenience-store bread sections. When you cut it, you count pieces as '한 조각' or '한 쪽'.

examples.en: I made fried eggs for breakfast.
Please put one more fried egg on top.
I put sausage and a fried egg in the lunch box.
A fried egg gets hard if you cook it too long.

examples.ko: 저는 노른자가 반쯤 익은 프라이를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like fried eggs with half-cooked yolks.

examples.ko: 밥 위에 프라이를 올리니까 더 맛있어졌어요.
examples.en: Putting a fried egg on the rice made it tastier.

explain: 한국에서 '프라이'는 대부분 '계란 프라이'를 줄인 말로 써요. 영어 fry보다 훨씬 좁은 뜻이라서, 감자튀김은 '프라이'가 아니라 '감자튀김'이나 '프렌치프라이'라고 해요.
explain_en: In Korea 프라이 mostly means 계란 프라이 in short, a much narrower sense than English fry. French fries are called 감자튀김 or 프렌치프라이, not just 프라이.

examples.en: I sprinkled ground pepper over the steak.
A pinch of ground pepper in the soup is enough.
We ran out of ground pepper, so I bought some at the mart.

examples.ko: 후춧가루 때문에 코가 간질간질해서 재채기가 났어요.
examples.en: The pepper made my nose tickle and I sneezed.

examples.ko: 식탁 위에 소금과 후춧가루와 설탕이 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Salt, ground pepper and sugar are on the table.

examples.ko: 후춧가루는 통후추를 갈아서 쓰는 게 더 향이 좋아요.
examples.en: Ground pepper smells better when you grind whole peppercorns yourself.

explain: 향신료 자체는 '후추'이고, 갈아 놓은 가루는 '후춧가루'예요. 알갱이 그대로는 '통후추'라고 해요. 말로는 그냥 '후추'라고 줄여 말하는 경우도 많고, 글로 쓸 때 사이시옷을 넣어 '후춧가루'라고 써요.
explain_en: The spice itself is '후추', and the ground powder is '후춧가루'. Whole peppercorns are '통후추'. In speech people often shorten it to just '후추', and in writing the word is spelled with a 사이시옷 as '후춧가루'.
